summary:
Developed by Team OffScale for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, the Mars Explorer - Smart Martian Map is a data-driven Martian terrain exploration system. It integrates multi-source NASA mission data, including topographic, spectral, thermal, and optical data, to provide a comprehensive view of Mars.

The project addresses the challenge of high-stakes Martian exploration by transitioning from standard terrain-aware navigation to human-aware navigation. It optimizes travel routes by accounting for critical human and environmental variables such as body mass, payload mass, local gravity, terrain conditions, and oxygen consumption.

This is vital because, unlike robotic rovers, human explorers face extreme conditions and unpredictable terrain where the shortest path is not necessarily the safest, and a wrong decision can jeopardize the entire mission. By prioritizing safe return-to-habitat planning and advanced hazard analysis, the system ensures the safety and long-term survival of human explorers.
details: Developed for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge, Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map is an autonomous bioenergetic navigation engine and real-time telemetry cockpit that safeguards astronauts during crewed Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) across Jezero Crater and Lower Mount Sharp on Mars. The platform fuses multi-instrument NASA orbital datasets, including MRO HiRISE 1 m/px elevation models, Mars Odyssey THEMIS nighttime thermal inertia, and USGS SIM 3464 geologic mapping, to synthesize a continuous 2D traversal cost field that prunes impassable >20-degree regolith cliffs, isolates sub-meter roughness, and flags sub-pixel orbital uncertainty. To achieve real-time flight execution, an isolated Euclidean Distance Transform scratchpad prevents NaN floating-point errors along cliff edges, allowing separable Sobel and discrete Laplacian operators to generate a shift-invariant Deviation Score that compresses the raster by 99.5% into an adaptive 1,200-vertex geometric graph validated via batched tensor collision checks. Crucially, rather than optimizing for abstract distance or time, our engine scales the Pandolf load-carriage biomechanical equation to Martian hypogravity (0.38 g), enforces an eccentric downhill muscle braking floor (>= 20%) to guarantee non-negative graph weights, and expresses directed edge costs directly in life-support Liters of Oxygen (O2) using the Weir calorimetry equivalent (20,100 J/L). Multi-leg trajectories are routed via a division-free directed A* algorithm that dynamically adapts as carried rock samples (0-30 kg) alter locomotion mechanics, while the life-critical Point of No Return (PNR) safety envelope is computed for all 1,200 nodes simultaneously in <3 ms using a single-source Dijkstra search on the reversed graph G^T outward from the Habitat with an enforced 1.15x safety margin. The engine is coupled to a dual-display human-machine interface combining a desktop Three.js WebGL Mission Control Cockpit, featuring multi-settlement replenishment scheduling, 3D Hab radio line-of-sight viewsheds, canyon-wall Solar Particle Event radiation shielding, and interactive NASA Perseverance rover ground-truth photo scouting, with a mobile smartphone HUD that streams real-time IMU gyroscope and compass orientation over full-duplex WebSockets to steer the 3D cockpit hands-free while delivering tactile throttles and audible/haptic emergency alarms. Developed in Python, JavaScript, NumPy, SciPy, and NetworkX, the entire end-to-end planning cycle executes in <25 ms on standard flight hardware, directly advancing NASA's Moon-to-Mars autonomy goals by transforming passive planetary topography into an active, life-critical bioenergetic guidance system.
